The entire team from reception, back office staff, nurses and Dr's have all proved outstanding in their care.

The fact that you can telephone or walk in any time of the day to make an appointment or raise a query and not have to complete an online form makes a huge difference and is very important to most patients.

Firstly, I have consistently found that doctors demonstrate a lack of attention to detail during appointments. There's a noticeable tendency to rush through consultations, which leaves little room for thorough assessment or discussion of health concerns. This approach often leads to a feeling of being unheard and can compromise the effectiveness of treatment.

Secondly, I have encountered what I perceive as discriminatory practices related to ADHD. The surgery refused to continue shared care for my ADHD, citing internal "policies." The communications I received, particularly via SMS, conveyed an impression of prejudice towards mental health conditions and mental disabilities. This stance has caused considerable distress and has significantly impacted my ability to manage a debilitating disability easily.

Finally, while I acknowledge the receptionists are generally satisfactory in person, phone interactions are often blunt and come across as rude. While I understand the need for efficiency, there is a clear opportunity for staff to maintain a more professional and empathetic demeanour when speaking with patients over the phone.
